summary.text: Amy Klobuchar, a member of the DFL, is Minnesota's senior U.S. Senator, first elected in 2006, and won the election for governor of Minnesota on November 3, 2026, defeating Lisa Demuth, according to unofficial results.
She previously served as Hennepin County Attorney.

paragraphs.text: Klobuchar was born in Plymouth, Minnesota, and grew up in the state, attending Wayzata High School.
She graduated magna cum laude from Yale University with a B.A. in political science in 1982 and earned a J.D. from the University of Chicago Law School in 1985.
Klobuchar worked as a corporate lawyer and partner at Minnesota law firms before entering public office.
She then headed the Hennepin County Attorney's office, the largest prosecutor's office in Minnesota, for eight years.
In 2006 Klobuchar was elected to the U.S. Senate, becoming the first woman elected to represent Minnesota there, and she has served since 2007.
She has since been sworn into a fourth term.
Her running mate was Ben Schierer, former mayor of Fergus Falls.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election for Governor of Minnesota with 55.5% of the vote to Lisa Demuth's 42.6% and Steven Young's 1.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
